properties.name: The first store-touching call of a session costs 26-48 s; a full export of the same store costs 2.1 s
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-21 while looking for something to optimise on the PRODUCT surface rather than the developer surface. This is the largest cost a user of reflow2 pays and nothing in the design mentioned it.

    open_questions    70 s   <- the SessionStart hook instructs every agent to call this FIRST
    loop_status       60 s   <- the server's own instructions call it "the one cheap call"
    graph_report      34-40 s
    detect_defects    33 s
    detect_gaps        3.2 s
    everything else  < 0.5 s

Two independent runs, consistent to within a second. **The call every session is told to make first costs a minute.**

⭐ IT IS ONE COST, PAID ONCE, NOT A COST PER CALL. The first store-touching call of a process pays it; every call afterwards — including the first call of a DIFFERENT node type — returns in 0.01-3 s. `scan_nodes(node_type: Question, limit: 5)` took 47.9 s and returned 8 KB; the same call immediately after took 0.02 s.

🛑 AND IT IS NOT THE DATA. A direct `--export`, which opens the store and reads every node and edge, takes **2.1 s** on the same 77 MB store. So the ~26-48 s is not RocksDB, not the volume, and not the disk.

TWO HYPOTHESES WERE FALSIFIED FIRST, both on a COPY of the store rather than the live one, which made the experiments free:
  (1) "It is the 999 LOG.old.* files." With them 2.07 s, without them 2.10 s. Falsified in thirty seconds.
  (2) "It is a stale rendezvous left by --stop-shared." On a pristine copy with no daemon and no rendezvous the first read still cost **26.3 s**. So ~26 s is INHERENT cold start; the ~48 s seen on the live store had roughly 20 s of stale-record timeout on top.

⭐⭐ THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT CRACKED IT, worth more than the finding: **47.91 s and 47.99 s across two runs is a TIMER, NOT WORK.** Real work varies with cache state and load; two runs agreeing to within 0.08 s means something is WAITING. That pointed at `READY_TIMEOUT` (30 s) and `RESPAWN_AFTER` (6 s) in shared.rs rather than at any algorithm.

WHERE THE REMAINING ~24 s LIVES, narrowed but NOT PROVEN: the gap between `--export` at 2.1 s and daemon startup at 26 s is whatever the server does that the exporter does not. shared.rs names the candidate in its own comment — "a cold daemon opens RocksDB and builds the full-text index, which on a large design is seconds, not milliseconds". A `fulltext` directory exists in the store (1.6 MB, 14 files), so something is persisted; whether it is rebuilt anyway, or validated, was not established.

📌 WHY NO TEST COULD HAVE FOUND THIS. The suite constructs graphs with `open_in_memory` and never opens the on-disk daemon path at all. 1393 tests pass in 96.5 s and not one of them touches the thing every real session waits a minute for. **The developer surface and the product surface were measured on the same day and were not the same system.**

🅿️ DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED. No budget has been stated for it, and the `optimize` skill written the same day says the budget comes before the code. This node is the measurement half; the target is owed.
